review_scope_note: Full-repository audit; the signing reviewer parsed the committed 3D result CSVs and logs, including the failure artifact, and inspected the 3D kernel's dealiasing and vortex-stretching terms.
verification_methods: Parsed the committed 3D CSVs: Kerr-type/TG run terminal BKM = 9.9895275659; random-IC 2000-step run BKM = 1.7619040326

Parsed run logs: 128^3 smoke run (BKM 1.243721, ~22.9 steps/s); 512^3 attempt terminates with 'CERTIFICATE_ERROR: cudaMalloc(...): out of memory' — a disclosed, machine-readable failure certificate rather than a silent absence

Inspected ns3d_bkm.cu: 2/3 dealiasing implemented as kmax = (N/3)*dk on all three axes, applied to all three RHS components; vorticity-form RHS includes the vortex-stretching term (the 3D-specific term absent in 2D)
Checked the finding's prose dealiasing description ('2/3 Orszag dealiasing') — stated correctly here, without the 2D page's mislabeled parenthetical

claim_reviews.claim: 3D vorticity-form pseudospectral solver with vortex stretching, cuFFT C2C, RK4, fp64, 2/3 dealiasing; BKM integral tracked.
claim_reviews.evidence: The kernel implements exactly this: three-component vorticity update with the stretching term, velocity recovered via u_hat = i(k x omega_hat)/|k|^2, correct N/3 dealias mask on all axes, RK4 stepping. The 3D methodological description matches the code.

claim_reviews.claim: Validation runs: TG/Kerr-type IC with BKM ~ 9.99; random IC with BKM ~ 1.76; 128^3 smoke run ~ 22.9 steps/s.
claim_reviews.evidence: All three recompute from committed artifacts (9.9895, 1.7619, 1.2437/22.9 steps/s). No NaN/Inf in the certified runs.

sources.reference: Committed 3D result CSVs and run logs

claim_reviews.claim: 512^3 is currently out of reach on the available single GPU (out-of-memory), disclosed as a limitation.
claim_reviews.evidence: The committed log shows the cudaMalloc failure emitted as a CERTIFICATE_ERROR line — the failure is preserved as an artifact, exactly per the project's data-preservation ethos. Committing failed runs with machine-readable error certificates is a practice worth propagating to the other experiments.

claim_reviews.claim: Infrastructure framing: no blowup claim; the BKM criterion is the diagnostic for future 3D singularity searches.
claim_reviews.evidence: The page makes no regularity or singularity claim, which is correct: nothing in these short, viscous, moderate-resolution runs could support one. The Beale-Kato-Majda framing is standard and correctly cited.

sources.reference: Beale, Kato & Majda, Comm. Math. Phys. 94 (1984); Orszag (1971)

overall_assessment: Clean infrastructure work, correctly framed and fully artifact-backed: the kernel does what the page says (including the 3D-specific stretching term and a correctly-stated 2/3 dealias rule), all published diagnostics reproduce from committed CSVs/logs, and — notably — the 512^3 failure is committed as a machine-readable error certificate rather than omitted. That failure-preservation practice is the best evidentiary habit in the project.
recommendations: Adopt the CERTIFICATE_ERROR failure-artifact pattern project-wide (it would have prevented several disputes in the Zaremba cluster)
certification_justification: All claims verified against code and committed artifacts; honest scope; exemplary failure disclosure.
